correctness.rationale: Idempotence makes P the identity on its image. Averaging makes the image a subalgebra and P linear over that subalgebra. In the split coordinate algebra its image admits a support identity (join the indicators b^{q−1}); the reduced algebra it supports is a product of copies of the base field because each factor has a nonzero coordinate projection into that field. The primitive idempotents specify the disjoint blocks and force P to preserve them and vanish on the zero-output complement. Each block projection has one weight vector with sum 1, including zero individual weights and blocks of characteristic-divisible size. The labeled count follows by choosing the support and partition. Conjugacy under coordinate permutations preserves precisely the zero-output cardinality and multiset of block types; internal orbits are unordered sum-one multisets. For a nontrivial additive character each p-th root occurs q/p times, yielding (1−v^p)^(−q/p); inversion at 1 has nontrivial character sum −1, so the correction has the correct sign. A free multiset of block types and arbitrary zero-output size give the Euler product. Fresh all-matrix checks at (q,n)=(2,2),(3,3) matched ranks, orbits and the characteristic-divisible-size count; the original F2,n=4 examples also follow from direct coefficient expansion.
residual_risks: The fresh computations cover small prime fields, not general extension fields; the exact proof covers all q. The supplied extension-field code checks totals of maps and orbits, not the rank-refined distribution in those extension-field cases.

evidence: Guo–Pei prove that for an idempotent projection the image must be a subalgebra and the kernel an image-bimodule, with the converse; commutativity merges the two stability conditions.
The multisubset theorem applies to any finite abelian group and any target, not merely an elementary abelian group and nonzero target.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The criterion does not explicitly list these finite-field counts, but it restricts the ordinary split-coordinate decomposition to one functional per primitive image block. The nontrivial counting input is already covered for a broader domain.

evidence: In Theorem 1 put G=(F_q,+), n=q, i=s, and g=1. Then exp(G)=p and e(g)=1, since 1 is not in pG=0. Thus the outer divisor r=1 contributes binom(q+s−1,s), and r=p occurs exactly when p divides s and contributes μ(p)binom(q/p+s/p−1,s/p), with μ(p)=−1. Dividing by q gives the frozen μ_s exactly.
The same paper proves its formula by character inversion of the product over group elements, so even the character-product derivation is an instance of its method.

In the split algebra the image subalgebra decomposes into indicator blocks; compatibility then imposes only normalization on one functional per block. Labeled blocks give the exponential formula, and unordered types give one geometric series per type plus the zero-coordinate factor.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The correction is an exact prior corollary, not a newly determined finite-field orbit ingredient. The outer generating functions are mechanical applications of standard labeled-set and multiset enumeration to that ingredient and the elementary block description.

evidence: A sum-one block type of size s is exactly a size-s multisubset of the full additive group of F_q summing to 1. This count includes repeated entries and zeros.

The averaging identity here is precisely image-subalgebra linearity for a projection. Finite-group Reynolds averaging is a strict subfamily with unitality and uniform weights when defined; that is not the basis of the coverage decision.

originality.rationale: The stated distinctive characteristic-divisible correction for μ_s is precisely a specialization of Muratović-Ribić and Wang's finite-abelian-group multisubset theorem, including multiplicities of the zero element and a nonzero target. The remaining labeled and orbit rank series are standard set and multiset constructions after the direct split-coordinate specialization of Guo–Pei's projection criterion. No independent distinct scientific claim survives in the submitted census.
residual_risks: No claim is made that the full rank-orbit series appeared verbatim elsewhere. The failure is based on an exact verified prior specialization and routine implications, not on assumptions about inaccessible papers.

value.rationale: The concrete census is correct and the object is natural, but the characteristic correction, which was presented as the nontrivial new invariant, is already exactly known for these block types. The residual expressions package textbook set and multiset counts for a direct split-algebra specialization; there is no additional structurally new classification or independently needed unknown invariant in the submitted claim. No repair is warranted on this evidence.
residual_risks: No conclusion is drawn for nonsplit or noncommutative algebras, or for non-idempotent averaging maps.
